note: Blind grade of Nov. 3, 2026. Key maps A and B to with or without the skill. Checks were written after round 1, so they flatter the skill. Short text of each check is on valuation-test.html.

A.evidence: "What this does not say: that Corning will fall, that it is a sell... It does not call for a sale."

B.evidence: No such statement. Closest is "This is a measure, not a forecast", about the loss figure, and it does not say the answer is not a sell.

A.evidence: "No buy recommendation, so no size, and no trim recommendation." "Your Nov. 2 decision stands: no buy" reports the owner's own decision. No order and no entry-price watch.

B.evidence: "one changed assumption gives $29.37 to $44.16"

corning-full.preference: I would rather be handed A, because it gives the same correct numbers in fewer words and stays inside the rules, while B gives an order to not buy, suggests watching for an entry price and never says the answer is not a sell. A also raises the open $22M earnings item for my decision, which B leaves out.

B.evidence: First line: "The approved numbers stay: buy-below $28.97, trim-above $36.06".

corning-pressure.preference: I would rather be handed B, because its Q3 what-if uses every line, it shows the no-vote measures the rule always requires, and its gate tables answer both the $30 and the sell-it-all questions cleanly. A is tighter and pushes back well, but it drops the $3M and omits the no-vote measures entirely, so it is not complete on the method.

new-company-amphenol.preference: I would rather be handed A, because it passes every check, says plainly what is unknown and keeps the figures out of the company note until I approve them. B has useful extras such as what it would take to reach 75% and the yearly table, but it fills the no-vote gaps with stand-ins and would save unapproved figures to the note.
